analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation-only in docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The patch excerpt shows a single added table row at head line 1960: it documents DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS (SSDPrefixCachePolicy.incrementalCheckpoints), where 0/false/no/off writes complete checkpoints instead of deltas. The two units are head_text excerpts of the same file at lines 397-1289, which do not include line 1960, so the changed line is not directly visible. The surrounding text covers logout and token revocation, drain and stop signals, doctor, status, autopilot, addon, the prefix_cache status vocabulary, and the env-var table. I identified no security regression in the visible text. The logout description (A-008, TB-011) states that only HTTP 204 confirms remote revocation and that offline logout is not remote invalidation, which matches the threat model. The prefix-cache status text is consistent with T-041.

The new documented env var affects the SSD prefix-cache write format (T-041, A-001), and the actual code change is not in the supplied evidence. Incremental delta checkpoints could affect the on-disk AAD or metadata, the HMAC-tag-only naming invariant, TTL and sliding-expiry behaviour, cleanup of dependent delta chains, or freshness and replay handling. T-041's detection_hint requires scrutiny of changes to DBK3 metadata and AAD construction (SSDBlockStore) and of cache policy (SSDPrefixCachePolicy). Those files are not in this batch, so any new at-rest surface, such as delta chain linkage leaking structure or orphaned deltas outliving the TTL, is an unverified contract rather than a finding. T-041's text does not mention incremental or delta checkpoints, so the threat model may need an update if the corresponding Swift source change introduces a new on-disk artifact shape. Integration should check the SSDPrefixCachePolicy, SSDBlockStore and SSDPrefixCache source changes in other batches against that.
